findings.highlight: must carry out his daily routine of using “magic”.
findings.evidenceJa: 日課になっている“魔術”を行わなくてはならない。
findings.governingReading: Before midnight Shirou must perform his daily Magecraft practice, explicitly marked as 魔術.
findings.explanation: Magic again collapses the learnable technical category into the separate category 魔法 at the opening of the work's detailed system explanation.

findings.highlight: I stretch out and adjust my breathing.
findings.evidenceJa: 結跏趺坐に姿勢をとり、呼吸を整える。
findings.governingReading: Shirou assumes the full-lotus seated posture and regulates his breathing.
findings.explanation: Stretch out replaces a specific cross-legged meditative posture with extending or reclining the body, changing the physical preparation for his inward concentration.

findings.highlight: No, I really am hypnotizing myself. As I have no Magic Crest and no knowledge of magic, a spell is only a change to myself.
findings.evidenceJa: 否、それは本当に自己暗示にすぎない。魔術刻印とやらがなく、魔道の知識もない自分にとって、呪文は自分を変革させる為だけの物だ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou corrects himself: the familiar formula is no more than self-suggestion, serving only to transform his own state.
findings.explanation: Hypnotizing asserts a stronger psychological procedure than 自己暗示, while is only a change turns the spell's purpose into malformed predication.

findings.highlight: inserting a burning steel rod into my backbone. This metal rod
findings.evidenceJa: 背骨に焼けた鉄の棒を突き刺していく。その鉄の棒こそ
findings.governingReading: Shirou experiences a heated iron rod being driven through his spine; that iron rod is his single circuit image.
findings.explanation: Steel and then generic metal replace repeated 鉄, changing and then dropping the concrete material inside a deliberately sustained bodily image.

findings.highlight: I can finally become a magus.
findings.evidenceJa: ようやく自分は魔術使いとなる。
findings.governingReading: Once the artificial line connects, Shirou finally becomes a 魔術使い, a practitioner or user of Magecraft, not a 魔術師.
findings.explanation: Magus assigns the category that Kiritsugu explicitly distinguishes from 魔術使い on page22, creating an internal contradiction in this same explanation.

findings.highlight: something like a burning tong which cannot be seen or felt
findings.evidenceJa: 目に見えず手に触れられない“火箸に似たモノ”
findings.governingReading: Something like fire tongs, invisible and impossible to touch by hand, is being forced into Shirou's spine.
findings.explanation: Cannot be felt denies sensation altogether even though the passage centers on felt pain; burning tong also mistakes the compound 火箸 for a heated singular tong.

findings.highlight: A living magus who performed many marvels and had touched the very structure of the world.
findings.evidenceJa: 数々の神秘を学び、世界の構造とやらに肉薄し、奇跡を実行する生粋の魔術師。
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu was a true-born magus who studied numerous mysteries, drew close to the structure of the world, and performed miracles.
findings.explanation: The English merges studied mysteries and performed miracles into performed marvels, and living replaces 生粋, dropping both the learning process and the characterization of him as a genuine magus.

findings.highlight: no strength of Magic Circuit
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術回路とやらの多さも
findings.governingReading: Shirou lacked an inherited abundance or high count of Magic Circuits.
findings.explanation: Strength replaces circuit number, changing the innate variable the following genealogy explanation discusses.

findings.highlight: a small source, “od”, created inside oneself.
findings.evidenceJa: 生物の中で生成される小源に分かれる。
findings.governingReading: Od is the small source generated within living organisms, contrasted with mana filling the world.
findings.explanation: Oneself narrows a biological category to the individual human subject and makes the definition reflexive rather than organism-wide.

findings.highlight: It’s like a filter. A magus turns his body into a filter, sucks up the mana from the world around him, and changes it into something he can use. This filter is what we call a Magic Circuit.
findings.evidenceJa: それは濾過器のイメージに近い。魔術師は自身の体を変換回路にして、外界から魔力を汲み上げて人間でも使えるモノ、にするのだ。この変換回路を、魔術師は魔術回路と呼ぶ。
findings.governingReading: Filtering is the image for drawing mana, while the magus makes the body a conversion circuit that renders external mana usable; that conversion circuit is the Magic Circuit.
findings.explanation: The English calls the body and Circuit a filter, collapsing the source's distinction between an explanatory filter image and the actual conversion function.

findings.highlight: since I was raised in a normal family, I don’t have many Magic Circuits.
findings.evidenceJa: 普通の家庭に育った俺には、多くの魔術回路を望むべくもなかった。
findings.governingReading: From his ordinary upbringing, Shirou reasons that he could not reasonably expect many circuits.
findings.explanation: The English promotes an expectation based on family background into a stated fact about his actual circuit count before the text supplies that count.

findings.highlight: You die when you die, and you kill when you must.
findings.evidenceJa: 死ぬ時は死に、殺す時は殺す。
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu bluntly says that in this path, one dies when one dies and kills when one kills.
findings.explanation: When you must supplies moral or circumstantial necessity for killing, softening an uncompromising statement about what the path entails into justified compulsion.

findings.highlight: you must not use it in front of people, and you must not cease your practice even though it is difficult to learn. Well, I don’t really care if you break that one.
findings.evidenceJa: 人前で使ってはいけないし、難しい物だから鍛錬を怠ってもいけない。でもまあ、それは破ったって構わない。
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu gives secrecy and continued-practice rules, then says those may be broken because the other-directed-use rule is most important.
findings.explanation: That one makes the concession grammatically singular and leaves unclear which of the two preceding rules may be broken, damaging the stated hierarchy.

findings.highlight: I feel the iron rod in my backbone slide into place.
findings.evidenceJa: 鉄の棒が、入ってはいけないところにズレていく感覚。
findings.governingReading: A stray thought makes Shirou feel the iron rod shift toward a place it must not enter.
findings.explanation: Slide into place reverses a lethal misalignment into correct positioning, contradicting the emergency recovery and conditional death on the following page.

findings.highlight: Before me is a metal pipe. I will channel magical energy into it, perform the simplest magic, and reinforce its durability.
findings.evidenceJa: 目前にあるのは折れた鉄パイプ。これに魔力を通し、もっとも単純な硬度強化の魔術を成し得る。
findings.governingReading: The target is a broken iron pipe, and Shirou attempts the simplest enhancement of its hardness.
findings.explanation: Metal removes the specified iron, while durability replaces hardness with a broader resistance to wear or damage; both concrete properties of the test object change.

findings.highlight: the lungs stretched to the limit demand air.
findings.evidenceJa: 限界まで絞られていた肺が、貪欲に酸素を求める。
findings.governingReading: His lungs, constricted or wrung to their limit, greedily demand oxygen as the internal heat vanishes.
findings.explanation: Stretched reverses compression into extension and drops the greedy, oxygen-specific bodily image.

findings.highlight: It’s hard to improve something that already has form.
findings.evidenceJa: 元からカタチが有る物に手を加えるのは、きつい
findings.governingReading: It is difficult to alter or add to something that already has a completed form.
findings.explanation: Improve presupposes a beneficial result immediately before Shirou explains that intervention may lower the object's completeness and value.

findings.highlight: Adding unnecessary things will actually decrease the value.
findings.evidenceJa: 補強する筈の筆が、芸術品そのものの価値を下げる事もある
findings.governingReading: A brushstroke intended to reinforce the completed artwork may instead lower the artwork's value.
findings.explanation: Unnecessary invents a prior judgment that the addition is needless, and the English removes the failed-intention contrast and sustained artwork/brush metaphor.

findings.highlight: I can visualize something’s structure easily, so I can make the outside look like the original. But it’s empty inside
findings.evidenceJa: 物の設計図を明確にイメージできるが故に、外見だけはそっくりに再現できるのだが中身は空洞
findings.governingReading: Because Shirou can clearly imagine an object's design drawing, he can reproduce its outward form, but the substitute remains hollow and nonfunctional.
findings.explanation: Structure normally includes internal organization, so claiming he easily visualizes it and then produces an empty interior creates a contradiction absent from the more limited 設計図 image.

findings.highlight: I would probably have destroyed most of my body.
findings.evidenceJa: 内臓をほとんど壊していただろう。
findings.governingReading: Had his recovery been one breath later, Shirou would likely have destroyed most of his internal organs.
findings.explanation: Most of my body broadens a specific internal-organ injury into general bodily destruction and changes the concrete physiological risk.

findings.highlight: The first step of a magus is to accept death.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師にとって一番初めの覚悟とは、死を容認する事だ。
findings.governingReading: The first resolve or readiness required of a magus is to accept death.
findings.explanation: First step turns an inner 覚悟 into a procedural stage, weakening the psychological and ethical burden that Kiritsugu says sadly.

findings.highlight: A superhero is really selfish, huh…?
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方っていうのは、とんでもないエゴイストなんだ、か
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu calls an ally of justice an outrageous egoist, while Shirou concludes he must become that ally of justice.
findings.explanation: Superhero twice replaces the explicit justice relation at the point where the work defines its exclusionary moral paradox.

findings.highlight: A skilled magus only detects what’s important
findings.evidenceJa: 優れた魔術師は患部だけを捉え
findings.governingReading: A skilled magus isolates only the affected or defective part and channels energy into it without waste.
findings.explanation: What's important replaces a concrete diagnostic target with subjective salience, weakening the repair and treatment analogy governing precise Strengthening.

findings.highlight: My dream is to become a superhero.
findings.evidenceJa: ボクの夢は正義の味方になる事です。
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls the exact childhood line that his dream is to become an ally of justice.
findings.explanation: Superhero repeats the established substitution in the isolated callback, erasing the phrase whose recurrence structures the surrounding reflection.

findings.highlight: I don’t know what kind of a person a superhero should be.
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方っていうのが何者なのかは分からない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou does not know what an ally of justice really is.
findings.explanation: Superhero again removes justice, while what kind of a person… should be reframes ontological uncertainty as uncertainty about the expected qualities of a known role.

findings.highlight: How can I become a superhero?
findings.evidenceJa: 何をすれば正義の味方になれるんだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks Kiritsugu what he must do to become an ally of justice.
findings.explanation: Superhero repeats the category replacement in the direct question that closes five years of unresolved effort.

findings.highlight: Father
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=オヤジ char=2]切嗣
findings.governingReading: The visible text names Kiritsugu while the ruby makes Shirou read or address him as オヤジ, Dad or old man.
findings.explanation: Father replaces both layers with one formal kinship term, deleting the visible personal name and the rough, intimate performed address.

findings.highlight: I think being a superhero is different from just helping others.
findings.evidenceJa: 人助けと正義の味方っていうのは違うと思う。
findings.governingReading: Shirou believes ordinary helping and being an ally of justice are different, but cannot grasp how to realize that difference.
findings.explanation: Superhero replaces the justice-bearing side of the explicit contrast, making the difference sound like scale or genre identity rather than an unresolved ethical category.
